title: Soundbar No Sound? HDMI ARC and eARC Fixes by Brand
metaDescription: No soundbar sound? Use the TV's HDMI ARC/eARC port, turn on HDMI-CEC, set TV audio to the soundbar and format to PCM. Fixes for Sonos, Bose, Samsung, Vizio.
h1: Soundbar No Sound? How to Fix HDMI ARC and eARC
intro:
When a soundbar plays nothing from the TV, the cause is almost always one of four settings: the cable is in a TV HDMI port that is not marked **ARC or eARC**, **HDMI-CEC** is off, the TV's **audio output** is still set to its own speakers, or the **digital audio format** is one the bar cannot decode. Fix those in order and most soundbars, from Sonos to Vizio, start working.

This guide gives the steps, the CEC name each TV brand uses, a symptom table, brand-specific notes, and the difference between ARC and eARC.
quickAnswer: Plug the soundbar into the TV's HDMI port labelled **ARC or eARC**, turn on **HDMI-CEC** in the TV settings (Anynet+ on Samsung, SimpLink on LG, BRAVIA Sync on Sony), set the TV's speaker output to **HDMI ARC / receiver / external speaker**, and set digital audio out to **Auto** (or **PCM** if there is still no sound). Then unplug both for a minute and power the soundbar on before the TV.

sections.heading: How to fix a soundbar with no sound over HDMI ARC
sections.body:
1. **Use the ARC or eARC port on both ends.** Only one HDMI port on most TVs supports ARC; it is labelled ARC or eARC. Use the soundbar's HDMI ARC/eARC (TV) port, not an HDMI input.
2. **Turn on HDMI-CEC.** ARC depends on it. The setting has a brand name on each TV (table below).
3. **Set the TV's audio output to the soundbar.** Look for Sound Output, Speakers or Audio Output and choose HDMI ARC, Receiver, Audio System or External Speaker. Turn the TV speakers off.
4. **Set digital audio out to Auto or Bitstream.** If the bar stays silent, try **PCM**: every soundbar can play it, though you lose Dolby surround formats.
5. **Enable eARC if you have it.** Many TVs have a separate eARC mode switch that is off by default.
6. **Power-cycle in order.** Turn both off, unplug them for a minute, plug in and power the soundbar first, then the TV.
7. **Swap the HDMI cable.** For eARC use a cable certified High Speed with Ethernet or Ultra High Speed; a damaged or very old cable can pass video but not the ARC return.
8. **Update firmware** on the TV and the soundbar, then try again.
9. **Fall back to optical.** If ARC still fails, connect a digital optical cable and set the TV's output to optical. You lose lossless and some Atmos formats, but you get sound.

sections.heading: What is HDMI-CEC called on my TV?
sections.body:
| TV brand | HDMI-CEC setting name |
|---|---|
| Samsung | Anynet+ (HDMI-CEC) |
| LG | SimpLink (HDMI-CEC) |
| Sony | BRAVIA Sync / Control for HDMI |
| Vizio | CEC |
| TCL (Google TV) / Roku TV | HDMI-CEC / T-Link; on Roku TV, System > Control other devices (CEC) |
| Hisense | CEC Function |
| Philips | EasyLink |

Menu paths change with software updates; search the TV's settings for "CEC" if you cannot find it.

sections.heading: Soundbar problems: symptom, cause and fix
sections.body:
| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| No sound at all | Wrong port, CEC off or TV output on internal speakers | Steps 1–3 above |
| Sound from apps but not from a game console or Blu-ray | Format the TV cannot pass through ARC | Set TV audio out to Auto or PCM; for lossless formats use eARC |
| Sound cuts out every few seconds | CEC handshake or cable fault | Power-cycle in order, swap cable, update firmware |
| Lip sync is off | Processing delay | Use the soundbar's or TV's AV sync / audio delay setting |
| TV remote won't change soundbar volume | CEC off, or the bar has not learned the remote | Turn on CEC; set up the remote in the bar's app |
| Soundbar turns on but says no signal | Wrong source selected on the bar | Switch the bar to its HDMI ARC/TV input |
| No Dolby Atmos | Plain ARC with a lossless source, or TV set to PCM | Use eARC, set output to Auto/Bitstream |

sections.heading: Sonos, Bose, Samsung and Vizio soundbar fixes
sections.body:
**Sonos (Arc Ultra, Arc, Beam Gen 2).** Steps 1–4 first. In the Sonos app, check the bar's TV settings and that it is updated; the app also has audio delay (lip sync) and remote setup. The [Sonos Arc Ultra](/gear/sonos-arc-ultra/) and [Beam (Gen 2)](/gear/sonos-beam-gen-2/) connect by HDMI eARC, with optical via Sonos's adapter. To restart, unplug the bar, wait, and plug it back in. More on Sonos systems in our [Sonos home theater setup](/sonos-home-theater-review/) guide.

**Bose (Smart Soundbar, Smart Ultra).** Use the HDMI eARC port and the Bose app to confirm the TV input and update firmware. See [Bose home theater](/bose-home-theater-review/).

**Samsung (HW-Q series).** On a Samsung TV, turn on Anynet+ and select the soundbar as the sound output; Q-Symphony (bar and TV speakers together) only works with compatible Samsung TVs. On a non-Samsung TV, use the standard steps. See [Samsung home theater](/samsung-home-theater-review/).

**Vizio.** Press Input on the soundbar remote until the bar shows HDMI ARC, turn on CEC in the TV, and set TV speakers off. Entry bars like the [Vizio SV210Y](/gear/vizio-soundbar-se-sv210y/) list an HDMI ARC input, so step 4 (PCM) fixes most silent setups.

sections.heading: HDMI ARC vs eARC: what is the difference?
sections.body:
| | ARC | eARC |
|---|---|---|
| HDMI version | HDMI 1.4 and later | HDMI 2.1 |
| Bandwidth | Compressed audio only | Up to 37 Mbps |
| Formats | Stereo PCM, Dolby Digital, DTS, Dolby Digital Plus (including streaming Atmos) | Adds uncompressed 5.1/7.1 PCM, Dolby TrueHD (Atmos), DTS-HD Master Audio, DTS:X |
| Lip sync correction | Optional | Required |
| Needs CEC to work | Yes | Uses its own discovery, though CEC still handles remote control |

If you stream, ARC carries Atmos from apps like Netflix inside Dolby Digital Plus. If you play 4K Blu-rays through the TV, only [eARC](/glossary/earc/) passes lossless Atmos. See [HDMI 2.1](/glossary/hdmi-2-1/).

mistakes.title: Using a regular HDMI input on the TV
mistakes.body: Only the port marked ARC or eARC sends audio back to the soundbar.

mistakes.title: Leaving the TV's speakers on
mistakes.body: Some TVs keep playing through their own speakers until you change the sound output.

mistakes.title: Forcing bitstream to a bar that cannot decode it
mistakes.body: If the bar does not support a format the TV sends, you get silence. PCM always works.

mistakes.title: Skipping firmware updates
mistakes.body: TV and soundbar makers fix ARC handshake bugs in updates. Update both before buying a new cable.

faqs.q: Why is my soundbar connected but no sound?
faqs.a: Usually the TV's audio output is still set to its own speakers, HDMI-CEC is off, or the cable is in a non-ARC port. Fix those three settings first, then try PCM output.

faqs.q: How do I get my TV to play sound through the soundbar?
faqs.a: Connect to the TV's HDMI ARC or eARC port, turn on HDMI-CEC, and set the TV's sound output to HDMI ARC, receiver or external speaker.

faqs.q: Why does my soundbar keep cutting out?
faqs.a: An unstable CEC handshake or a poor cable. Power both devices off and unplug them, restart the soundbar first, try another certified cable and update firmware.
Yes for lossless audio: eARC carries Dolby TrueHD Atmos and DTS:X from Blu-ray. For streaming apps, ARC already carries Dolby Digital Plus Atmos.

faqs.q: Do I need a special HDMI cable for eARC?
faqs.a: A cable certified High Speed with Ethernet or Ultra High Speed works. Ultra High Speed is the safe choice for long runs and 4K120.

faqs.q: Can I use optical instead of HDMI ARC?
faqs.a: Yes. Optical gives you sound when ARC fails but carries only compressed 5.1 and stereo, not Atmos or lossless formats, and the TV remote may not control the bar's volume.

bottomLine: Most silent soundbars are fixed by four settings: the **ARC/eARC port**, **HDMI-CEC on**, **TV output set to the soundbar**, and **audio format on Auto or PCM**. Power-cycle in order, swap the cable and update firmware if that fails, and use optical as a fallback. If you are replacing the bar, see the [best soundbar for home theater](/best-soundbar-for-home-theater/); for Sonos systems, the [Sonos home theater setup](/sonos-home-theater-review/).
